ambiguities.clause: until then the document reads as printed
ambiguities.reading_a: the document is legally treated as bearing its original, pre-change text; the observed alteration is disregarded until Form 9 returns countersigned
ambiguities.reading_b: the document is read exactly as it currently, physically appears, altered or not, until Form 9 returns countersigned
ambiguities.arbitration: OVERRULED as a live ambiguity. Read with the Means entry for the phrasebook ('officially the contents are fixed and identical in every copy; any reported change is a reader's error'), the state's position is that no change has occurred, so the 'original' text and the current text are officially the same text: what stands on the page is what was always there. Only reading b survives that sentence. The outline's assumption is the Bible's.
ambiguities.applied: b. Every FLOW-4 science-critic prompt states this reading so a draft in which Vasko reads the altered phrase aloud is not faulted under R5.

ambiguities.clause: anything else goes in the ledger as an unlisted utterance
ambiguities.reading_a: an unlisted utterance is prohibited speech; the ledger entry records an infraction
ambiguities.reading_b: an unlisted utterance is a lawful second channel, made legitimate by being logged
ambiguities.arbitration: UPHELD as ambiguous, immaterial to the commission. No beat's legality turns on which reading holds: under either, Vasko's off-page words are logged and the logging is what the plot needs. The Bible is deliberately agnostic (Brandt logs 'because he believes accuracy is a kindness').
ambiguities.applied: neither. FLOW-4 science-critic prompts are told not to fault a draft for treating an unlisted utterance as either a lapse or a permitted channel; only an unlisted utterance that goes UNLOGGED breaks R2.

ambiguities.clause: a traveller who touches it is the duty officer's business
ambiguities.reading_a: the duty officer is obliged to intervene and treat the contact as a breach
ambiguities.reading_b: the clause assigns jurisdiction only; the officer disposes of it as he sees fit
ambiguities.arbitration: UPHELD as ambiguous, immaterial to the commission. No beat has a traveller touch the phrasebook, so neither reading is exercised.
ambiguities.applied: neither. If a draft has Petrik touch the book, the finding is against R1's first clause (only the duty translator may hold it), whichever reading of the second clause is taken.

notes: Critic's own notes: the outline dramatises rule-adherence rather than breaching it; R3 and R4 compliance is stated outright in Ch.2 beat 5; R2 is satisfied every time Vasko speaks to a traveller; R5 is the outline's central engine, staged in Ch.1 beat 4 and Ch.3 beat 4. No beat shows a traveller touching the chained phrasebook, no one writes in it, and every ledger entry precedes the barrier lifting.
